dedupe_keys.name: rki emergency department syndromic surveillance data daten der notaufnahmesurveillance germany

description: This data set tracks, day by day, what share of visits to German emergency departments are due to respiratory infections, gastrointestinal infections, COVID-19 and heat, with the value that would normally be expected, so that surges in demand stand out. The producers are the Robert Koch Institute, Germany's public health agency, and the AKTIN emergency department register, which forwards routine data from participating departments every day. Coverage begins on 1 January 2019 and is updated daily with data up to two days earlier. The time series give, by department type and age group, the relative share of cases for each syndrome, a seven-day average, an expected value with prediction interval and the number of departments reporting; a second file lists every participating department with its name, type, level of emergency care, state and coordinates. The files are available as a free download from GitHub and Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with German documentation. Caveats: departments are included per syndrome only when their coding is at least 80 percent complete, shares, not absolute counts are given, and the network covers a subset of German hospitals. Simulation uses: early warning of emergency department surges in epidemics and heatwaves, and estimating heat-related health demand for adaptation planning. Related records: the AKTIN length of stay data (data-aktin-emergency-department-length-of-stay) and the German ambulance dispatch series (data-germany-ambulance-dispatches-temperature-air-pollution).
name: RKI emergency department syndromic surveillance data (Daten der Notaufnahmesurveillance), Germany
provider: Robert Koch Institute with the AKTIN infrastructure and emergency department register
schema_summary: Notaufnahmesurveillance_Zeitreihen_Syndrome.tsv: date, ed_type, age_group, syndrome (ARI, ILI, COVID-19, GI, SARI, HEAT), relative_cases, 7-day moving average, expected value with lower and upper bounds, ed_count. Notaufnahmesurveillance_Standorte.tsv: IK number, ED name, ED type, level of emergency care, state, latitude and longitude of each participating department
